title: Academic Cybersecurity Assurance
scope: Student Lab Board; local fictional-data classroom instance. Public/private-student deployment is a separate risk scenario.

frameworks.name: OWASP Top 10
frameworks.role: Awareness categories organize risk discussions; they are not test requirements.

frameworks.name: OWASP ASVS
frameworks.role: Selected requirements define concrete verification targets; this is not a full ASVS assessment.

frameworks.name: MITRE CWE
frameworks.role: Weakness taxonomy links design/code causes to mitigations.

frameworks.name: MITRE ATT&CK
frameworks.role: Adversary behaviors help build abuse cases. A scenario mapping does not prove an attack occurred.

controls.title: Trusted-service input validation
controls.reason: FluentValidation rejects blank titles and missing booleans through the API; malformed, length-boundary and missing-resource cases also run in HTTP verification. The selected test is not all-input coverage.

controls.title: Context-appropriate rendering
controls.reason: The experiment-title DOM sink uses textContent and the tested markup remains literal. Scope is this rendering path, not every possible HTML context.

controls.title: Avoid dynamic evaluation
controls.reason: Three local Semgrep rules inspect application sources for HTML sinks, dynamic JavaScript evaluation, and process execution. A clean pattern scan is limited SAST evidence, not complete data-flow analysis.

controls.title: Function and object authorization
controls.reason: The classroom board intentionally permits anonymous shared reads/writes. It does not meet a private-board authorization requirement; add identities and server-enforced ownership before that deployment.

controls.title: Anti-automation and resource limits
controls.reason: A request-size limit exists, but total item count, creation rate, and memory growth are unbounded. No high-volume denial-of-service test was executed.

controls.title: Generic unexpected-error responses
controls.reason: ProblemDetails and exception handling are configured. No unexpected exception has been deliberately exercised; validation errors do not prove this requirement.

controls.title: Protected, useful security logs
controls.owasp: A09:2025 Security Logging and Alerting Failures
controls.reason: Local evidence hashes detect accidental artifact changes. There is no protected, actor-attributed application security audit trail; local file hashes are not an audit-log control.

controls.title: Dependency inventory and vulnerability monitoring
controls.asvs: supporting supply-chain evidence; no full requirement claim
controls.reason: Runtime Zod and FluentValidation plus development/test packages are inventoried. npm and NuGet advisory checks cover known advisories at scan time; provenance, continuous monitoring, and zero-day exposure remain outside this run.

threats.title: Shared-board modification without an owner
threats.scenario: If deployed as private student boards, an anonymous caller can change or delete another student's item because there is no identity/ownership boundary.
threats.attackContext: Integrity-impact analogy; in-memory classroom items are not a demonstrated adversary campaign or persisted enterprise data.
threats.next: Implement identity/ownership and run anonymous, owner, and non-owner API cases.

threats.title: Stored input reaches an HTML execution sink
threats.scenario: A future innerHTML regression could turn a saved experiment title into executable markup.
threats.attackContext: No ATT&CK technique assigned: an XSS weakness alone does not establish a specific adversary execution behavior.
threats.next: Retain literal-rendering regression and Semgrep sink rule across new rendering paths.

threats.title: Repeated creation exhausts memory
threats.scenario: Small individually valid requests can grow the board without a global cap; the request-body limit does not cap total memory.
threats.attackContext: Endpoint availability abuse scenario; resource exhaustion was not executed.
threats.next: Add item quotas/rate limits and verify bounded rejection using a small deterministic case.

threats.title: A vulnerable dependency becomes reachable
threats.scenario: An affected Zod, FluentValidation, or tool version could introduce a reachable vulnerability; a package advisory requires version/configuration/reachability analysis.
threats.attackContext: Only relevant if a remotely exploitable feature is publicly exposed. Current localhost operation is not evidence of public-facing exploitation.
threats.next: Review advisories, confirm affected paths, upgrade deliberately, and retest normal/negative behavior.

riskMethod: Classroom ordinal likelihood × impact, each 1–5. 1–4 low, 5–9 moderate, 10–14 high, 15–25 critical. These are explicit teaching estimates for the stated deployment scenario, not CVSS, probabilities, or accepted risk. Residual likelihood is used only when its linked runtime/advisory evidence exists; impact stays unchanged.
